title: Next-Token Prediction Basics
description: Explains LLMs as systems that repeatedly predict the next token. Covers probability distributions, generated continuations, why fluent text can still be unsupported, and how application context changes the next-token prediction loop.

title: Base, Instruction, And Chat Models
description: Compares base language models, instruction-tuned models, and chat models. Covers role formatting, supervised fine-tuning, assistant behavior, system messages, and when each model type is useful.

title: Transformer Block Intuition
description: Introduces transformer blocks with self-attention, feed-forward layers, residual connections, and normalization. Focuses on engineering intuition rather than mathematical derivation.

title: Attention And Long-Range Context
description: Explains how attention helps tokens use information from other tokens in the prompt. Covers references across long passages, prompt sensitivity, and why changing context changes model behavior.

title: Logits And Decoding Settings
description: Explains logits, probabilities, greedy decoding, temperature, top-k, and top-p sampling. Covers deterministic extraction tasks, creative generation, reproducibility, and output variance.

title: Context Windows As Working Memory
description: Explains context windows as the visible working memory of an LLM call. Covers system instructions, examples, conversation history, retrieved documents, user input, and generated output space.

title: Model Memory Versus External Sources
description: Clarifies the difference between information encoded in model weights and information supplied through databases, APIs, tools, and retrieval systems. Covers why LLMs are not reliable databases.

title: Prompt Structure And Message Roles
description: Explains how prompt task, context, constraints, examples, and output format shape behavior. Covers system, user, and assistant roles as text that becomes tokens.

title: Tokenization Basics
description: Introduces tokens as model text units. Covers words, subwords, punctuation, whitespace, special tokens, vocabulary IDs, and why one word is not always one token.

title: Tokenization Of Code And JSON
description: Shows why code, JSON schemas, URLs, tables, and punctuation-heavy prompts can use many tokens. Covers output schemas, structured prompts, and formatting tradeoffs.

title: Prompt Budgeting
description: Builds a prompt budget across system instructions, examples, conversation history, retrieved context, user question, and reserved output tokens. Covers context-window fit decisions.

title: Token-Based Cost Estimation
description: Explains input tokens, output tokens, per-million-token pricing, request cost, high-volume cost, and why cost is a product-design variable.

title: Latency And Long Context
description: Explains how long prompts and long outputs can increase latency. Covers shortening prompts, reducing repeated instructions, and choosing only relevant context.

title: Conversation History Management
description: Explains how chat history consumes context window space. Covers truncation, summarization, message selection, and when old turns should be dropped.

title: Retrieved Context Budgeting
description: Explains how retrieved chunks consume input tokens. Covers chunk count, chunk size, answer space, and cost tradeoffs in retrieval-augmented generation.

title: Output Length Planning
description: Explains why applications must reserve output tokens. Covers concise answers, structured output, max token limits, and failure modes when the answer has no room.

title: Bag Of Words Foundations
description: Introduces bag-of-words representations as transparent text vectors. Covers term counts, vocabulary, word order limitations, and interpretability.

title: TF-IDF Intuition
description: Explains term frequency inverse document frequency. Covers common words, informative words, document frequency, sparse vectors, and why TF-IDF is useful for local practice.

title: Neural Embeddings Overview
description: Explains neural text embeddings as dense learned vector representations. Covers semantic similarity, multilingual behavior, domain fit, and differences from keyword systems.

title: Cosine Similarity
description: Explains cosine similarity as a direction comparison between vectors. Covers normalized vectors, score interpretation, top-k ranking, and why scores are relative.

title: Embedding Query Design
description: Explains how query phrasing affects vector search. Covers short queries, verbose queries, exact terms, semantic paraphrases, and ambiguous questions.

title: Chunking Strategies
description: Explains why documents are often split into chunks before embedding. Covers chunk size, overlap, section-aware splitting, and context preservation.

title: Embedding Metadata
description: Explains why vectors need metadata such as source, title, section, timestamp, owner, and document ID. Covers filtering, citations, debugging, and auditability.

title: Embedding Failure Modes
description: Covers keyword mismatch, semantic drift, chunk boundary problems, outdated sources, weak metadata, and misleading similarity scores.

title: Semantic Search Architecture
description: Builds the high-level semantic search pipeline: documents, preprocessing, embeddings, vector storage, query embedding, similarity calculation, ranking, and result review.

title: Top-k Retrieval
description: Explains why applications inspect top-k results rather than only top-1. Covers top-3 context, downstream prompts, and rank-based debugging.

title: Manual Relevance Labels
description: Explains how to label expected topics or expected source documents for retrieval evaluation. Covers small golden sets and realistic support questions.

title: Recall At k
description: Explains recall@k for retrieval evaluation. Covers whether relevant context appears in the first k results and why recall@3 is useful for RAG.

title: Mean Reciprocal Rank
description: Introduces reciprocal rank and mean reciprocal rank. Covers giving more credit when the first relevant result appears near the top.

title: Precision At k
description: Introduces precision@k and relevance density in retrieved results. Covers cases where returning many weak chunks can hurt generation.

title: Confidence Thresholds
description: Explains how retrieval thresholds support fallback behavior. Covers weak top scores, unrelated questions, clarification requests, and escalation paths.

title: Hybrid Search
description: Explains combining keyword and vector search. Covers exact terms, semantic meaning, code identifiers, product names, and reranking candidates.

title: RAG Pipeline Overview
description: Introduces retrieval-augmented generation as retrieval plus prompt construction plus answer generation. Covers source grounding, citations, and external memory.

title: Prompt Construction For RAG
description: Explains how retrieved chunks are inserted into prompts. Covers separators, source IDs, instructions, context ordering, and answer constraints.

title: Citation And Source Grounding
description: Explains why RAG answers should cite or reference retrieved sources. Covers claim support, source IDs, unsupported claims, and review workflows.

title: RAG Fallback Behavior
description: Explains what a system should do when retrieval is weak. Covers no-answer decisions, clarification, routing to humans, and confidence communication.

title: RAG Evaluation Layers
description: Covers evaluating retrieval, prompt construction, answer grounding, citation quality, latency, cost, and user feedback separately.

title: Document Freshness In RAG
description: Explains how stale documents create stale answers. Covers update workflows, re-embedding, source timestamps, and removing old vectors.

title: Vector Store Operations
description: Introduces vector store responsibilities: storing vectors, metadata, IDs, filters, deletes, updates, and approximate nearest-neighbor search.

title: Reranking Retrieved Results
description: Explains reranking as a second-stage selection step after initial retrieval. Covers retrieving many candidates and selecting stronger context for the prompt.

title: Hallucination Risk
description: Explains hallucination as fluent unsupported or fabricated output. Covers why language quality is not the same as factual support.

title: Bias And Representation Risk
description: Explains bias risks from training data, prompts, retrieved documents, and evaluation sets. Covers subgroup review and harm analysis.

title: Stale Knowledge
description: Explains how model weights and indexed documents can become outdated. Covers retrieval freshness, APIs, and source update workflows.

title: Privacy And Sensitive Data
description: Explains privacy risks in prompts, retrieved context, logs, and generated outputs. Covers filtering, minimization, redaction, and access controls.

title: Prompt Injection
description: Explains prompt injection through user input or retrieved documents. Covers instruction hierarchy, treating retrieved text as data, and defensive parsing.

title: Unsupported Claims
description: Explains how to detect and handle factual claims that are not supported by context. Covers citations, refusal, and answer review.

title: Low-Confidence Outputs
description: Explains what to do when retrieval scores, classification scores, or model self-checks are weak. Covers fallback and escalation.

title: Monitoring LLM Systems
description: Covers production monitoring signals: latency, token cost, fallback rate, low-confidence retrieval, bad feedback, and citation coverage.

title: Golden Test Sets
description: Explains small curated evaluation sets for ordinary, ambiguous, unsafe, unrelated, and adversarial inputs. Covers expected behavior before implementation.

title: Retrieval Regression Tests
description: Explains how to catch retrieval quality regressions using labeled queries and expected top-k documents or topics.

title: Answer Grounding Review
description: Explains reviewing generated answers against retrieved context. Covers claim support, citation correctness, and unsupported additions.

title: Output Format Validation
description: Explains checking structured outputs such as JSON, labels, and tables. Covers deterministic prompts, parsing, and validation errors.

title: Safety Evaluation Cases
description: Explains adversarial and unsafe test cases, including prompt injection, secret requests, harmful instructions, and privacy-sensitive inputs.

title: Human Feedback Loops
description: Explains how user feedback, support review, and annotation loops improve LLM applications over time.

title: Cost And Latency Monitoring
description: Explains tracking token usage, request cost, long-tail latency, and budget alerts for LLM-powered products.

title: Release Readiness For LLM Features
description: Covers final readiness checks: evaluation set results, fallback behavior, logging, monitoring, rollback plan, and owner review.

title: Support Router Project Overview
description: Introduces the support-routing exercise combining token count, cost estimate, local retrieval, confidence decision, and risk explanation.

title: Support Question Data Audit
description: Guides practitioners through inspecting support questions, expected topics, difficulty labels, ambiguous cases, and unrelated questions.

title: Support Router Token Estimate
description: Guides practitioners through estimating token count and cost for support questions plus retrieved lesson descriptions.

title: Support Router Retrieval Results
description: Guides practitioners through recording top-1 and top-3 lesson candidates, scores, and relevance notes.

title: Support Router Threshold Choice
description: Guides practitioners through testing thresholds, identifying false fallback decisions, and writing a threshold justification.

title: Stakeholder Explanation
description: Guides practitioners through explaining the system to non-technical stakeholders, including what it does, why it can fail, and how to monitor it.

title: Support Router Extension Ideas
description: Suggests extensions such as source URLs, citation output, logging, fallback categories, and larger relevance sets.

title: Final Reflection
description: Prompts practitioners to connect tokens, embeddings, semantic search, retrieval evaluation, and risk analysis into one application mental model.

title: Prompt Compression Strategies
description: Covers shortening instructions, removing repeated boilerplate, using compact schemas, and moving deterministic logic into application code.

title: Few-Shot Example Tradeoffs
description: Explains when examples improve behavior and when they waste context. Covers representative examples, concise examples, and output consistency.

title: Multilingual Embedding Considerations
description: Explains how multilingual queries and documents affect embedding model choice, evaluation examples, and source metadata.

title: Domain-Specific Vocabulary
description: Explains why specialized product names, acronyms, code identifiers, and course labels can challenge generic embedding systems.

title: Retrieval Debugging Checklist
description: Provides a debugging checklist for bad retrieval results: query wording, document text, chunking, metadata, model choice, filters, and thresholds.

title: RAG Answer Policy
description: Explains answer policies for grounded assistants: cite sources, state uncertainty, refuse unsupported claims, and ask clarification when needed.

title: Evaluation Report Template
description: Shows how to summarize retrieval and answer-quality results for reviewers, including pass criteria, failures, and next actions.

title: LLM Application Debugging Map
description: Maps common failures to layers: input, prompt, retrieval, model, decoding, parser, storage, monitoring, and user feedback.
